ai.name: Anthropic
ai.hook: Fable writes its own GPU kernels, an early sign of AI improving its own tooling.
insights: Import AI calls it **"the first genuine, fastest megakernel ever"** written by an AI model
Signals a nascent **recursive self-improvement loop**: model helps build the tools that build better models
Comes right after Fable's cybersecurity-safeguard relaunch, now routing some requests to Opus 4.8
ai.for_you: No direct action here for the agency today, but worth tracking: if models start writing their own optimized infra, the tooling gap between 'uses AI' and 'AI builds its own stack' widens fast, and that's the gap your agency needs to stay ahead of for clients.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Most significant capability signal in Import AI this week, distinct from routine model releases

ai.name: Simon Willison
ai.hook: Shipped a semver-safe major release almost entirely via Claude Fable for $149 in API costs.
insights: **sqlite-utils 4.0rc3** adds compound foreign key introspection, a breaking change he'd been avoiding for years
Used Claude Code for web on iPhone to do the final pre-release review
Total cost across rc1-rc3 iterations: **~$149.25** in API spend for what would've been days of manual work
ai.for_you: This is your agency's pitch made concrete: a solo operator shipped a real, breaking-change library release for under €150 in AI costs. Use this exact framing (cost + before/after) as a case study slide for PT SMB clients who doubt AI can touch 'real' engineering work.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Most concrete, dollar-quantified proof point of solo+AI shipping this week

ai.name: Interconnects (Nathan Lambert)
ai.hook: GLM-5.2 marks a real capability threshold for open-weight agents, not just a cheaper option.
insights: Framed as a **step change**, not incremental: open models crossing into genuinely usable agentic territory
Coincides with Tencent's Hy3 release (295B MoE, 21B active) directly competing with GLM-5.2
Separate op-ed argues **banning open source AI would be a mistake**, co-authored for a general audience
ai.for_you: Open models hitting frontier-agent quality means your agency can build client-facing agents on GLM-5.2 or Hy3 self-hosted, cutting per-token costs to near zero for high-volume PT SMB use cases like customer support bots.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Best synthesis of why open models matter now vs. just another release announcement

ai.name: Tencent
ai.hook: Tencent's Hy3 open-weights model beats rivals 2-5x its size, running natively on vLLM.
insights: **295B MoE** total, only **21B active parameters**, 192 experts, **256K context**
Apache 2.0 licensed, built from feedback across 50+ products since a preview in April
Up to **2.95x speedups** on NVIDIA/AMD via MTP speculative decoding
ai.for_you: Another self-hostable option to benchmark against GLM-5.2 for cost-sensitive PT SMB deployments where you control the inference stack rather than pay per-token to a US lab.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Concrete open-weight release with real benchmarks, not just a teaser

ai.name: Natalia Quintero
ai.hook: A non-technical consultant now uses Codex to automate her CRM and manage her father's medical care.
insights: Resisted Codex for months before daily pestering from Dan Shipper converted her
Still pays for Attio and Asana rather than vibe-coding replacements, even while building custom tools elsewhere
Manages an internal AI agent ('Claudie') that requires human oversight, not full autonomy
ai.for_you: This is your target client persona exactly: a non-technical operator who'll pay for AI-built internal tools but won't replace core SaaS. Frame your agency's pitch to PT SMBs around the same boundary, custom automation around their existing tools, not a full rebuild.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Only episode this week showing a non-technical user's real build workflow, directly maps to Pedro's client profile

ai.name: Vercel (Guillermo Rauch / Andrew Qu)
ai.hook: Vercel bets agents and models are splitting into a separate layer developers must design for.
insights: New agent framework **eve** treats skills, sandboxes, and agent-readable websites as first-class concerns
Argument: the model is commoditizing, the orchestration layer around it is where value concentrates
Ties into a broader theme this week (Latent Space, AIEWF) of coordination, routing, and memory as the new UX battleground
ai.for_you: This validates the agency's positioning: sell PT SMBs the orchestration and integration layer around commodity models, not a proprietary model. That's the defensible, higher-margin part of the stack.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Clearest articulation of a structural shift echoed across three separate sources this week

build_this.name: OfficeCLI
build_this.what_it_is: A CLI letting AI agents directly read and edit Microsoft Office files (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
build_this.why_try_it: Most PT SMB clients live in Excel and Word, not Notion or Airtable. Wire this into a client automation this week, e.g. an agent that reads invoices from Excel and drafts a Word report, and you have a demo that lands instantly with non-technical owners.

build_this.name: Ternlight
build_this.what_it_is: A 7MB embedding model that runs entirely in-browser via WASM, no server round-trip.
build_this.why_try_it: Drop this into the yoga/meditation platform for instant client-side semantic search, e.g. searching past sessions or journal entries by meaning, with zero backend cost or latency.

build_this.name: sqlite-utils 4.0 (AI-assisted release workflow)
build_this.what_it_is: A documented, reproducible workflow for using Claude Code to ship a real breaking-change software release cheaply.
build_this.why_try_it: Steal the prompt pattern from his blog post ('final review before shipping a stable release') for your own micro-SaaS experiment this week, it's a ready-made checklist for using Claude/Codex to get to a confident v1.0 without needing to be the one writing every line.

podcasts.episode: The Most Innovative Diffusion Research Is Happening in Drug Discovery, Not Image Generation
podcasts.takeaway: Diffusion models now simulate proteins physically flexing to bind drugs, a much harder problem than static pose prediction.
key_points: Genesis's PEARL model predicts both binding location and protein flexibility simultaneously
The team argues the field's favorite benchmark, 2Å RMSD, is largely misleading
Their agentic system SAPPHIRE reasons like a chemist: hypotheses, literature reading, next-round candidate proposals
podcasts.for_you: No direct action for Pedro's current bets, filed for awareness as a signal of where the most technically serious AI work is happening outside chatbots and coding agents.
